summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload disguised as ESLint config
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint TypeScript configuration but ships a preinstall hook (scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs") that performs alternate-runtime code execution at install time. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style minified (renamed hex identifiers, stringified property lookups) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip into a temp directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, and uses execFileSync to invoke the Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript payload using a rotating string-array pattern (WV8StW / n7gIxM) with hex-obfuscated identifiers. Neither the downloaded Bun runtime nor the math_init.js payload has any relationship to the package's declared ESLint-configuration purpose. Executing the obfuscated payload under an alternate runtime bypasses Node-based install-time scanners. The combination of purpose mismatch, obfuscated launcher, alternate-runtime dropper, and obfuscated sibling payload executed at install time with the installer's privileges is a supply-chain attack fingerprint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
